Overview / 03#

Intelligence is not the experience.

Work IQ supplies workplace understanding. Each experience decides how to use it.

Work IQ / intelligence

Permission-aware work context, retrieval and reasoning, plus supported tools for agents.

Copilot, Cowork & Scout / experiences

The interfaces and workflows people use to ask, delegate and coordinate.

Studio & Foundry / agent platforms

Authoring and runtime services plan work, select tools and execute the agent’s workflow.

Not a model or standalone chat app

Work IQ is not itself the model, runtime or harness that runs every agent.

Not a new home for all enterprise data

Existing systems remain sources of record. Connections and permissions must be configured.

Not governance—or an access grant

Agent 365 supports oversight; Entra and Purview supply identity and data controls. Work IQ does not bypass them.
Read moreWork IQ overview · Copilot Studio harness · Agent 365 overview

Overview / 04#

One intelligence layer. Five ways to use it.

The contribution is shared; the experience, execution path and availability are not identical.

Microsoft 365 Copilot

Ask and understand.

Work-grounded answers, summaries and meeting preparation inside Copilot.

Copilot Cowork

Delegate an outcome.

Multi-step work across messages, meetings and Office artifacts, with steering and approval.

Microsoft Scout

Keep coordination moving.

Desktop Frontier preview connects work context with local tools and ongoing tasks.

Copilot Studio · GitHub harness

Build a repeatable agent.

The GitHub Copilot harness orchestrates; a configured Work IQ connection adds workplace understanding.

Microsoft Foundry (Azure AI Foundry)

Extend a custom agent.

A preview connection brings Microsoft 365 understanding into a domain-specific workflow.

Shared Work IQ contribution

Context + reasoning + supported tools.

Experiences consume these capabilities differently. No automatic cross-product handoff is implied.

Capabilities / 05#

From work signals to useful understanding.

Three conceptual building blocks explain what Work IQ brings to an agent.

01 / Data

The work around a question.

Files, emails, meetings, chats and configured business systems provide relevant signals.

WHERE TO WORKMicrosoft 365 + connected sources

User access determines what can be reached.

02 / Context & memory

Meaning, not just matching words.

Relationships, priorities and supported memory help connect people, projects and previous work.

WHERE TO WORKWork IQ workplace understanding

Continuity depends on the consuming experience.

03 / Reasoning & tools

Turn context into a useful response.

Models, skills and permitted tools help answer questions or support the next action.

WHERE TO WORKSupported agent capabilities

Tool requests remain user-scoped and policy-evaluated.

Business valueAn agent can work from a connected picture rather than make the user restate the background.

Permissions apply throughout. “Memory” does not mean one universal store automatically synchronizes every agent or client.

Capabilities / 06#

Four surfaces. Choose the help you need.

Chat, Context, Tools and Workspaces are ways to consume the intelligence—not competing architectures.

Chat

Get a grounded answer.

Returns a processed, Copilot-style response; supports continuity and delegation.

Example Explain a project’s open decisions with supporting sources.

Context

Prepare your agent to reason.

Assembles relevant workplace inputs instead of requiring raw signals to be stitched together.

Example Supply project background to a service agent.

Tools

Do permitted work.

Agent-friendly access to mail, calendar, files, people, chat and sites.

Example Find a document or perform an enabled operation.

Workspaces

Keep task working material.

SharePoint Embedded storage for intermediate data and outputs inside the Microsoft 365 tenant boundary.

Example Preserve a task’s draft and working files.

Business valueUse a ready-made answer, agent-ready context, permitted actions or persistent task storage—without treating them as the same thing.

Copilot: get ready for the decision.

Use workplace context to turn a broad question into a focused, source-backed answer.

Example / meeting readiness

“Before the steering meeting, summarize what changed on Project Phoenix, the unresolved decisions and the evidence I should read.”

What Work IQ contributes

Capabilities / 08#

Cowork: delegate the outcome, not each step.

Cowork plans and executes multi-step work; Work IQ supplies the workplace context.

Example / a meeting packet

“Create a steering-meeting packet from this week’s project updates. Include decisions, risks and a draft agenda. Show me the draft before sharing.”

How the work moves

Gather relevant context → plan the task → produce documents and proposed actions. The user can pause, steer and review.

WHERE TO WORKMicrosoft 365 Copilot → Cowork

Sensitive actions use approval controls. Cloud execution and local browser integration are distinct capabilities.

An example of context becoming a working document—not a claim of measured customer results.

Capabilities / 10#

Scout: keep coordination moving.

Work context meets a desktop agent with local tools, continuing tasks and user control.

Example / prepare on a schedule

“Each Monday, prepare a private brief of the week’s project meetings, missing inputs and decisions to revisit.”

WHERE TO WORKScout desktop → scheduled tasks

Value: Make preparation a repeatable routine rather than a fresh search.

Example / close the loop

“After the review, compare the notes with my local action tracker. Draft reminders for items without owners; ask before sending.”

WHERE TO WORKScout → Microsoft 365 + local tools

Value: Connect collaboration context with the files and tools where follow-through happens.

Who does what

Work IQ: workplace context about priorities and collaboration.

Scout: orchestration, memory, schedules, local files, shell and browser capabilities.

User: granular permissions, steering and sensitive-action approval.

Availability: Windows/macOS desktop is Frontier preview. The cloud always-on expansion is a private-preview path—not a universal GA capability.

Capabilities / 12#

Foundry: bring work context to a custom agent.

Microsoft Foundry combines domain logic with a configured, preview Work IQ connection.

01 / Ask a business question

Example A service-readiness agent asks: “What has the launch team agreed, and which customer commitments remain unresolved?”

WHERE TO WORKFoundry project → agent

The agent also has its own approved business tools and domain instructions.

02 / Delegate the work question

Work IQ retrieves, reasons over and synthesizes relevant Microsoft 365 context using the signed-in user’s delegated permissions.

WHERE TO WORKSettings → Connections → Work IQ

Configure the connection, then attach the capability to the agent.

03 / Combine and respond

The custom agent combines the returned understanding with its domain evidence to prepare a readiness brief.

WHERE TO WORKCustom workflow → reviewable output

Value: Avoid making business context and workplace context separate conversations.

Boundary matters: Foundry and Work IQ are distinct services. Requests may leave the Azure compliance boundary; Foundry may process or store returned Microsoft 365-grounded responses. Review end-to-end residency.

Business valueFoundry IQ supplies curated knowledge grounding; Work IQ supplies workplace understanding. They are complementary, not interchangeable.

Hook up Work IQ: identity before prompts.

Custom Foundry route · integration preview · one-time admin setup, then reusable agent configuration.

1 / Establish the trust

Entra + Microsoft 365 administrators

Provision the Work IQ service principal. Register a single-tenant, bring-your-own Entra app; grant delegated WorkIQAgent.Ask and admin consent.

Enable Copilot Credits billing for the API path. General Work IQ API billing is separate from Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing.

2 / Configure the connection

Foundry → Settings → Connections → New → Work IQ

Supply the tenant/app and required OAuth settings. Add the returned OAuth redirect URI to the Entra app.

Use an approved secret store for credentials; never embed secrets in prompts or slides.

3 / Attach and prove access

Toolbox → Work IQ built-in tool → agent

Attach the reusable toolbox MCP to the agent. At runtime, Foundry routes the request to Work IQ via A2A using the signed-in user’s delegated identity.

Test one allowed and one denied source before enabling broader use.

Connection values from Learn
Targethttps://workiq.svc.cloud.microsoft/a2a/
Scopesapi://workiq.svc.cloud.microsoft/WorkIQAgent.Ask offline_access
No app-only access for this Work IQ connection. Foundry User / Project Manager roles let people work in Foundry; they do not grant access to another user’s files. Start read-only; test write scopes and approvals separately.

Capabilities / 17 HOW · Revision 22 September 2026#

Add Fabric and Foundry IQ deliberately.

Choose the route for the question. A native Cowork shortcut is not an ontology integration.

A / Direct Fabric IQ connection

Foundry integration · preview

Publish the selected ontology, semantic model or data agent. Authorize the user and source access; copy that item’s endpoint.

Create the Fabric connection, add the tool to a toolbox and attach it to the agent. Ontology/model paths use delegated OBO: bring-your-own Entra app or managed OAuth.

For a bring-your-own ontology app: consent to delegated Item.Execute.All, Item.Read.All and offline_access.

B / Ontology in Foundry IQ

Alternative knowledge-base route · preview

Prepare Azure AI Search and the documented managed-identity RBAC prerequisites.

Foundry → Knowledge → Knowledge bases → New. Select a Fabric IQ source; use the OneLake picker to choose an accessible ontology.

Name and describe the source/base; set retrieval and answer instructions. Attach the base to the agent; test entity-grounded citations. This is not mandatory duplicate ingestion.

C / Native Copilot Cowork

Fabric IQ plugin · preview

The plugin is installed by default. Attach, paste or name a Power BI report, ask a question, then chain results into document or mail tasks.

Queries run as the user; item permissions and row-level security apply. This route grounds on reports/backing semantic models—not arbitrary ontologies, lakehouses or eventhouses.

Direct read-only Power BI MCP is a separate GA route; delegated identity preserves RLS/OLS.

Do not generalize authentication. Foundry data-agent connections are delegated too; only the separate direct data-agent MCP client supports a service-principal option. Foundry IQ ACLs are source-specific, not universal inheritance.

Capabilities / 18 HOW · Revision 22 September 2026#

Identity is checked at every resource.

Documented flow + proposed safeguards · a delegated token is not blanket permission to enterprise data.

  1. Entra sign-inThe user signs in. Apply the configured identity/access policies for that user and application.
  2. Agent chooses a toolFoundry runtime roles control agent use/configuration—not mailbox, file or Fabric access.
  3. Per-resource delegationWork IQ uses on-behalf-of (OBO) user identity; Fabric uses its own configured connection. OAuth consent permits calling a service, not reading every item.
  4. Source + policy checksEvaluate user permissions and supported labels/policies. Fabric item permissions and model RLS/OLS remain relevant; Foundry IQ needs source-specific ACL setup.
  5. Filtered evidence returnsPass allowed facts with citations to the agent. Proposed control: missing or denied evidence stays missing—no higher-privilege fallback.
  6. Controlled outputRestrict recipients and storage; enable downstream protection, logging and retention. A synthesized answer does not carry source ACLs automatically.

Revocation is not instantaneous

Consent revocation stops further permission grants; existing tokens can remain valid until expiry. Test membership/policy propagation and token expiry explicitly.

Boundaries do not disappear

Foundry may process/store Work IQ responses. A shared tenant does not prove residency; Fabric can return cross-region data. Private Foundry ingress does not privatize Work IQ’s public endpoint.
Evidence / LearnWork IQ: authentication / security boundaries · Fabric IQ: identity / region · Foundry IQ: access control · Purview for Foundry

Build a business ontology—not a mail copy.

Proposed Project Phoenix design · illustrative entity names, IDs and properties; not actual tenant data.

Entity typeStable key + typed propertiesDirected relationship / source of truth
ProjectprojectId: string
status: string; ownerId: string		Project HAS_RISK → Risk
Authoritative project register
DecisiondecisionId: string
projectId: string; state: string		Decision FOR_PROJECT → Project
Approved decision register
RiskriskId: string
projectId: string; severity: string		Risk FOR_PROJECT → Project
Approved risk register
PersonpersonId: stringProject OWNED_BY → Person
Governed identity reference
PolicypolicyId: string
version: string; effectiveDate: string (ISO date)		Project GOVERNED_BY → Policy
Approved policy catalog; content via controlled retrieval

Agree the meaning before binding

A business owner approves canonical IDs, definitions, synonyms, metrics and ambiguity rules. “Phoenix” is a display name; PRJ-PHX is the illustrative join key.

Link evidence without granting access

Map source IDs/URLs and evidence dates to canonical entities. Query work evidence under the current user’s permissions; a URI or relationship never grants access. Do not copy full mail into a common store.

Capabilities / 21 HOW · Revision 22 September 2026#

From prepared sources to a tested graph.

Fabric ontology preview · build a bounded pilot; keep security and financial semantics intact.

1 / Prepare and choose the path

Data engineer + Fabric admin

Enable the Fabric capacity and tenant prerequisites. Prepare governed sources, unique string/integer keys and a relationship mapping table.

Create from an existing Power BI semantic model or manually bind prepared OneLake data. Use approved isolated, nonsensitive pilot data where preview limits require it.

2 / Review and bind explicitly

Business owner + ontology author

Review generated names, typed properties, keys and entity definitions. Confirm every property’s source binding.

Define each relationship’s origin and target types. Bind both IDs from the mapping table; save. Validate uniqueness, missing targets and ambiguous joins.

3 / Refresh, release and test

Data engineer + QA owner

Upstream changes require manual graph refresh for these relationship bindings. Set and test a freshness SLA; do not promise universal real-time updates.

Publish only after entity/relationship queries pass. Native ontology versioning is unavailable: use an external change log, reviewed release and rollback plan.

Generation is not full model migration

Import/DirectQuery generate definitions—not bindings or query execution. Direct Lake supports bindings under constraints. Measures/calculated columns are not carried into ontology queries. Keep authoritative financial measures and RLS on the semantic-model path; graph decimal support is currently absent.

Do not weaken production security

Current static bindings require managed lakehouse tables without column mapping and without OneLake security enabled. Do not disable security on sensitive production tables. Choose an approved isolated pilot or a supported alternative path; time-series bindings have separate prerequisites.
Evidence / LearnCreate ontology: two paths · Binding prerequisites / limitations · Relationships / refresh · Generation limits · Ontology FAQ / versioning

Capabilities / 22 HOW · Revision 22 September 2026#

Engineer a context packet, not a giant prompt.

Proposed assembly contract · combine just enough authorized evidence to answer this user’s question.

1 / Resolve the business identity

From the governed Fabric path

Resolve Project Phoenix to a canonical project ID and relevant entities. Set the requested time window and “as of” time. Reject ambiguous or wrong-project matches.

2 / Retrieve evidence and policy

Separate Work IQ + Foundry IQ calls

Ask Work IQ for relevant work evidence under the current user. Retrieve the approved policy/version via a configured Foundry IQ source. Apply supported ACLs; reject stale policy.

3 / Reconcile, cite, then respond

Agent-side rules, not automatic IQ merging

Distinguish authoritative state from conversation. Flag conflicts and missing evidence. Every material statement needs a source or an explicit “not established.”

Minimal packet passed to synthesis

Identity + scope
Canonical entity IDs
User/access scope • time window
Evidence + provenance
Allowed facts • source IDs/links
Evidence timestamps • policy versions
Handling + uncertainty
Sensitivity / destination constraints
Freshness • conflicts • denied/missing sources
Safe memory is an explicit design. Isolate user/session caches; minimize retention; recheck access when reusing evidence. Treat retrieved instructions as untrusted data. Never keep unrestricted full mail in the ontology or a common vector store. Work IQ Workspaces are not a blanket cross-agent memory service.

Capabilities / 23 HOW · Revision 22 September 2026#

Trace one steering-committee question.

Illustrative test scenario—not observed results: “Can Project Phoenix pass its next approval gate, and why?”

01

Resolve → Fabric IQ

Resolve the project ID; query project state, open risks and decisions from the selected ontology. Query governed financial measures through the semantic model—not the graph.

Check: wrong ID or mismatched role → stop / deny
02

Explain → Work IQ

Ask for recent authorized decisions and supporting OneDrive, SharePoint and email evidence tied to that ID. Return source links and evidence dates—not unrestricted mailbox exports.

Check: private or DLP-blocked item → exclude
03

Interpret → Foundry IQ

Retrieve the approved gate policy and effective version from the configured knowledge base. Cross-check applicability; do not silently substitute a stale policy.

Check: stale or denied policy → no definitive verdict
04

Reconcile → agent, then reviewer

Draft a cited assessment: established facts, conflicting evidence, missing checks and recommended next step. Do not equate lack of visible risks with no risks.

Check: recipient access + human approval before sharing
Proposed fail-closed behavior: “Readiness is not established from the evidence available to you.” Explain the missing category without disclosing denied content. Do not retry with an admin identity. A read-only assessment does not approve the project or send a message.
Evidence / LearnFabric IQ: query selected item · Work IQ: user-delegated retrieval · Foundry IQ: entity-grounded citations

Capabilities / 25#

Permission-aware does not mean permission repair.

The controls remain distributed across the services that own identity, data, runtime and spend.

Microsoft 365 admin center

Work IQ availability & spend.

Set tool availability, permitted writes and spending policies for supported integrations.

Microsoft Entra

Identity & access.

Apply the user and agent access controls required by each supported connection.

Microsoft Purview

Data controls.

Apply the relevant information protection, data governance and compliance policies.

Agent 365

Agent oversight.

Inventory and govern integrated agents. Work IQ intelligence does not replace this control plane.

Power Platform admin center

Studio environments & usage.

Manage the environment and monitor Copilot Studio credit consumption.

Microsoft Foundry

Connections & runtime.

Review delegated access, returned data, processing boundaries and separate runtime costs.

Work IQ tools are user-scoped, logged and policy-evaluated. Clean up oversharing first; scope writes and approvals. A shared Entra tenant does not, by itself, prove end-to-end data residency.

Chapter 02 · Ground agents in your business process.

Business skills—build, manage and use business skills so Copilot and agents understand your business processes.

Scenario / low-code maker

Business Process Owner @ Caldova Capital · Copilot Studio · Power Apps Maker Portal

“Caldova needs additional vendors to meet growing demand. We can find the expansion opportunities—but deciding which vendor meets our standards still depends on scattered guidance and individual expertise. I want to capture our vendor-selection process once, maintain it as our requirements change, and let people use it across Copilot and agents—without rebuilding it for each experience.”

Pain point / the process is scattered

The steps, decisions and exceptions rarely live in one place:

  • With individual experts — experience, exceptions, who to ask
  • Across documents — policies, checklists, decision criteria
  • Inside systems — app logic, workflows, business records

Someone has to stitch it together. Every time.

Build once. Use across agents.One shared business skill (vendor selection: decision criteria · process instructions · supporting resources) → Work IQ → Copilot Studio purpose-built business agents and custom/coding-agent experiences using Work IQ MCP

Business valueDifferent agents. The same business process—captured in a business skill, not a separate copy inside every agent.

Value / 38#

Measure business outcomes, not just usage.

The value is plausible and testable. These are recommended measures—not claimed results.

Relevance

Potential value: answers reflect the actual project and its evidence.

Measure: source correctness, decision relevance and correction rate.

Continuity

Potential value: less repeated briefing within a supported workflow.

Measure: repeated context entry, unresolved handoffs and owner coverage.

Completed work

Potential value: usable documents, trackers and approved actions.

Measure: acceptance rate, rework and end-to-end task completion.

Reuse & integration effort

Potential value: less custom context assembly across agents.

Measure: retrieval work avoided, maintenance effort and cost per accepted output.

Business valueStart with a baseline and a bounded scenario. Compare output quality, control effectiveness and total cost before scaling.

Activity counts are adoption signals—not proof of ROI, compliance or decision quality.
Read moreWork IQ overview · Work IQ APIs · Work IQ for agents

Adoption / 39#

Adopt by scenario. Budget by execution path.

Start with one workflow: clean up access, test quality and controls, limit spend, then measure.

Native experience ≠ custom API use

Applicable Copilot experiences include Work IQ. Custom/third-party API calls are metered separately; general API access does not itself require a Copilot license.

Budget the complete workflow

Cowork and the Studio harness use usage-based billing. Foundry adds runtime/model charges. Connector prerequisites and user entitlements may also apply.

WHERE TO WORKM365 admin: Work IQ policies
PPAC: Studio credit usage · Foundry: runtime

Work IQ APIs: GA. Studio Work IQ and Foundry integration: preview. Cowork: work/school GA. Scout desktop: Frontier preview. Regions and entitlements vary.
